gần mực thì đen, gần đèn thì rạng
gần mực thì đen, gần đèn thì sáng

flags.why: Gạch đít means physically underlining text, not figuratively emphasising an idea.
Parboiled rice is gạo đồ, not gạo đỏ, as defined in the [rice standard](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/linh-vuc-khac/van-ban/tieu-chuan-quoc-gia-tcvn-128472020-ve-gao-do-42072.html).
The entry omits the everyday meaning of folding something in half.
flags.fix: verb | to fold in half; ex: Gấp làm đôi tờ giấy này. = Fold this sheet of paper in half.

flags.why: A learner is most likely to encounter this phrase as an instruction to fold something in half.
The English example leaves the animal's Vietnamese name untranslated.
flags.fix: The sloth bear has a long snout like a pig's.

flags.why: Gấy meaning 'wife' is regional Nghệ Tĩnh vocabulary, as documented in the [Nghệ Tĩnh dictionary](https://nghengu.vn/tieng-nghe-cua-toi/tu-dien-tieng-nghe-tinh-van-e-g-h-i-k-l-m-n-1184.html).

The idiom means maliciously making false accusations to harm someone, rather than simply passing responsibility, as explained in this [dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/gắp_lửa_bỏ_tay_người).
flags.fix: to make false accusations against someone to bring trouble upon them

flags.why: The translation adds 'He botched the job,' which the Vietnamese does not say.
flags.fix: He maliciously accused his colleague, blaming everything on them.

flags.why: The phrase describes acknowledging someone else's superiority, not being far superior oneself.
flags.fix: to acknowledge someone as far superior to oneself

flags.why: Xịn gọi bằng cụ is not a natural way to describe a phone's quality.
flags.fix: Về khoản chơi cờ, tôi phải gọi anh ấy bằng cụ. = When it comes to playing chess, I have to acknowledge that he is far better than me.
